verdict.rationale: Auth0's own Actions feature runs versioned Node.js functions that customize login and identity flows, including signup and login flows that store metadata. It replaces the older Rules and Hooks, and code can be shared across Actions. That covers custom logic running automatically during identity events, but the evidence never lists the trigger points or describes an event-to-action rule model beyond login and signup. missing for 10: documented list of event triggers (e.g., post-login, pre-registration, M2M), evidence of event-driven automation beyond login/signup flows, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Actions are a more secure, tenant-specific, versioned Node.js functions that let you customize your login and identity flows.
Reduce the amount of custom code and time to build and maintain solutions, by upgrading from Rules and Hooks to Auth0 Actions.
Build custom signup and login flows to prompt users for additional information and store it as metadata on the Auth0 user profile.
This feature allows you to create, manage, and share reusable code across different Actions within your Auth0 Tenant.
